comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C15-C21 regarding SNP density, recombination rate effects on IBD detection, and reliability concerns. Both evaluations find these claims well-supported by Figure 2 data. OpenEval emphasizes the logical flow of conclusions while peer reviewers highlight the convincing nature of the evidence with explicit endorsements from all three reviewers and the editor.

Complete concordance on claims C22-C24 about comparative performance of IBD callers. Both evaluations support the findings based on Figure 3 data. OpenEval focuses on the consistency of metrics (FN/FP rates) while peer reviewers explicitly confirm hmmIBD as the best tool, making this a central finding that is unquestioned.

Full agreement on claims C25-C29 regarding parameter optimization benefits for human-oriented callers. Both evaluations find the dramatic improvements well-documented in Figure 4. OpenEval emphasizes the grid search methodology while peer reviewers highlight the practical recommendations and accept the optimization results without challenge.

Strong concordance on claims C30-C33 about downstream applications (selection detection and population structure inference). Both evaluations support these findings based on Figure 5 supplement data. OpenEval provides technical detail on metrics while peer reviewers accept these applications as part of the comprehensive benchmarking without critique.

Complete agreement on claims C34-C40 regarding Ne estimation performance and hmmIBD superiority. Both evaluations find strong support in Figure 5 data. OpenEval details the mechanistic explanations and TMRCA filtering benefits while peer reviewers emphasize the reliability concerns and central importance of hmmIBD for quality-sensitive analyses.

Full concordance on claims C41-C47 about empirical validation using real P. falciparum data. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing. OpenEval emphasizes how empirical data strengthens simulation conclusions while peer reviewers highlight the well-structured study design and the importance of tailoring tools to species characteristics.

Perfect agreement on claims C48-C50 regarding computational efficiency comparisons. Both evaluations accept the runtime and memory usage findings from Figure 7. OpenEval notes the implementation detail about hmmIBD's single-thread limitation while peer reviewers acknowledge the computational trade-offs as part of comprehensive benchmarking.

Strong concordance on claims C51-C53 representing main conclusions and recommendations. Both evaluations find these well-supported by the comprehensive analyses. OpenEval justifies the hmmIBD recommendation based on accuracy-sensitive analyses while peer reviewers provide explicit endorsements from all reviewers and editor, calling the study 'important' and 'meaningful contribution.'

Agreement on claims C1-C2 providing malaria background context. Both evaluations find these appropriately cited and supported. OpenEval notes standard WHO citation while peer reviewers initially requested more emphasis on P. falciparum importance, which was addressed in revision, leading to acceptance of this framing.

Complete concordance on claims C3-C8 about IBD applications in malaria genomics. Both evaluations find these background claims well-cited and accepted. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations to published research while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the utility of IBD for selection detection, Ne inference, and population structure analysis.

Perfect agreement on claims C9-C14 regarding key genomic differences between P. falciparum and humans. Both evaluations find these claims well-supported and central to study rationale. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and logical inference while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge these characteristics as the interesting case motivating the research.

Full concordance on claims C54-C58 about demographic and evolutionary parameters used in simulations. Both evaluations find these well-established and appropriately cited. OpenEval emphasizes literature support while peer reviewers implicitly accept these parameters through their endorsement of the simulation approach without questioning parameter choices.
